pages.text: The following glyphs act on entities, allowing practitioners to distinguish, sort and detect entities of different types. Some return booleans depending on the type of entity fed, while others are meant for detection, and return lists of entities. For further details, research Minecraft’s entity classification system.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.is_animal
pages.text: $(n)entity$() → $(n)boolean$()$(br)Pops an entity and returns true if it is classified as an animal.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.is_hostile
pages.text: $(n)entity$() → $(n)boolean$()$(br)Pops an entity and returns true if it is classified as hostile (monster).

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.is_item
pages.text: $(n)entity$() → $(n)boolean$()$(br)Pops and entity and returns true if it is classified as an Item entity.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.is_player
pages.text: $(n)entity$() → $(n)boolean$()$(br)Pops an entity and returns true if it is classified as a player.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.is_living
pages.text: $(n)entity$() → $(n)boolean$()$(br)Pops an entity and returns true if it is classified as a ‘living entity’.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.is_mob
pages.text: $(n)entity$() → $(n)boolean$()$(br)Pops an entity and returns true if it is classified as a mob.

pages.title: glyph.lingua_mundi.zone_entity
pages.text: $(n)vec, num$() → $(n)list$()$(br)Pops a number and a position vector. Sweeps a sphere of radius equal to the popped number and returns a list of the entities found within that region. The list may be empty, and will never contain more than 256 elements.
